arc_two_years_of_paper.description:
Eight requisitions, and I copied every one. Powder, iron, two smiths and a healer, and the last one just says 'anything'.

The Elder can't send a column up a road we haven't walked. He can send this, and this says the city knows they're there. Don't tell me that's nothing. For two years it was nothing, and now it isn't.
arc_two_years_of_paper.accept_text: Hand it to him yourself and watch his face. I'd like to know what two years of waiting looks like.
arc_two_years_of_paper.turn_in_text:
It's been two years.

I'm going to read this properly, and then I'm going to put it on the wall of the longhouse, where everyone who's still angry about it can see the date on it. Thank you for carrying it. Go and see the Quartermaster.

org_binding_invoker.description: I've spent a lifetime learning where a warlock's contract ends. Jergosh the Invoker has built a chamber in the chasm, and a cult round the idea that it never ends at all, and Voidwalkers he didn't earn walk his ritual hall. I recognise the mistake, because I made it myself twenty years ago, and I don't want to see it made again on the scale of a city. The way down is Ragefire Chasm, in the south-west corner of the city, a long walk from my door, and Jergosh's chamber lies north of the lake. Mind the Voidwalker Minions, because they're his hands, and he's never once had to use his own.
org_binding_invoker.accept_text: When he falls, break the circle, and don't read what's in it.
org_binding_invoker.turn_in_text:
The circle's broken, so the debt's paid, at least in part.

Take this with you. A better warlock than me used to carry it, and I'd be pleased if you turned out better than either of us.

org_cinderfang.description: I don't hunt for sport. I hunt what threatens the herd, and a salamander the size of a wolf has taken to the shores of the lava lake beneath the city. The troggs call it Cinderfang, and they keep their distance. I keep a list of the animals I've failed to bring home, and the list is short, and I'd like it to stay that way. The lake's in Ragefire Chasm, in the south-west corner of the city, and it lairs on the north-east shore, where the Cinder Salamanders will lead you to it.
org_cinderfang.accept_text: Keep to the stone, don't touch the lava, and don't run.
org_cinderfang.turn_in_text:
That's a clean kill. I've seen that pelt on a trogg's wall once, and I won't again.

Choose whichever piece you'll use. I'd only hang it on a wall.

org_embers_beneath.description: The warm vents under the Cleft of Shadow used to be only warm. For a month now they've been loud with picks and drums, and there's a smell of sulphur that doesn't belong to nature. Troggs who haven't come near the city in a generation are streaming up out of Ragefire Chasm, and something with a purpose is behind them. I don't like things with a purpose I haven't given them. Go down through the Cleft and kill the Ragefire Troggs, and the Ragefire Shamans who keep them loud, then come back and tell me what the chasm has become.
org_embers_beneath.accept_text: I won't send a tide of warriors into a place I don't understand. Be my eyes down there first.
org_embers_beneath.turn_in_text:
So it isn't only troggs. I'd rather know that than not, and the Cleft's quieter already.

But something down below is feeding that fire. Take this, and listen to me again.

org_hexed_ash.description: The Searing Blade doesn't burn its offerings for flavour. The ash is a reagent, the reagent is a curse, and a curse needs a hand. I've spent a week analysing the ash my customers brought back, and every sample points the same way, down the chasm, to a priestess called Acolyte Zhurra Bloodhex. The pyromancers and cultists in Ragefire Chasm, across the city in its south-west corner, carry the ritual ash, and Zhurra holds the altar in the antechamber, behind the cages. Bring me the ash and put her down, because she's the one who makes it mean something.
org_hexed_ash.accept_text: Don't touch the ash with bare skin. I mean that as an apothecary, not a worrier.
org_hexed_ash.turn_in_text:
I won't ask what you saw. I'll say that the sample matches, and her curse is broken at the root.

I'd like you to have something from my own stock.

org_hunger_in_the_lake.description: The cultists didn't find the lava lake. They found what lives in it. Taragaman the Hungerer is an elemental older than this city, and for ten thousand years he's done nothing but burn and wait. Someone has been feeding him, binding him, and pointing him at Orgrimmar, and I won't have a bound spirit of that size waiting under my city like a fuse. Ragefire Chasm opens in the south-west corner of the city, so follow the west wall south from this hold until the ground turns warm, and beyond the antechamber you'll find the lake with two stone bridges across it and Taragaman where they cross.
org_hunger_in_the_lake.accept_text: Don't fight him on the bridges for longer than you must. The lake is his, and he'll use it.
org_hunger_in_the_lake.turn_in_text:
The Hungerer's gone. I felt the vents go quiet from here, and for the first time in a month the city's breathing right.

There's still the one who held his chain.

org_new_border.description:
Go up to the escarpment, the long drop where the Lift's cliff used to be. Garuk Emberhide has been on it a season and will give you the short version, which is the only version he has.

The harpies are what the Elder cares about. Barrens harpies are roosting on a mountain, nesting on bare rock instead of the crags they hatched in, and my wind riders won't fly near them. Thin them where you find them and count what you see.
org_new_border.accept_text: Keep your rider low over the drop. The wind off that cliff comes up hard and without warning.

org_ore_deep.description: I keep one piece of black rock above my anvil, and I've been staring at it for a week. It came from the mining spur under the Cleft, and it's the best ore I've ever put a hammer to. I want more of it. The troggs digging it up and the elementals warming it down below are a very small obstacle, the way I see it. It's down in Ragefire Chasm, south of my forge, in the corner where the city wall meets the rock, so bring me lumps of it, black and shot with orange.
org_ore_deep.accept_text: You'll know it when you pick it up, because it'll want to burn your hand. Wear thick gloves.
org_ore_deep.turn_in_text:
Look at that grain. I could make a blade from this that would sing, and though it won't be today, I won't forget who brought it.

Here's something from the racks.

org_pitbreaker.description: The best ore in the spur belongs to a trogg called Grulgash. He isn't a warlord. He's a miner with a miner's grudge, and a hammer that's broken more pit-props than I've forged blades. Nobody mines the black seam while Grulgash the Pitbreaker is breathing, and I'd pay a fair bit to see that change. Go back down Ragefire Chasm, south of my forge, west of the warrens past the supply racks, and kill the Ragefire Diggers first, because they keep him informed.
org_pitbreaker.accept_text: He's bigger than he looks and angrier than he sounds. Don't let him swing that hammer twice.
org_pitbreaker.turn_in_text:
The seam's open, and I'll have the smiths down there before the week's out.

As for his hammer, I don't need it, and you do. Choose whatever you want from the racks.

org_sinister_edge.description: Every cult needs a blade, and the Searing Blade's is a trogg-hater named Bazzalan. He sits on an obsidian throne at the end of the chasm, in a hall that was an orc shrine before it was theirs. He doesn't shout and he doesn't pose. He waits for you to look at the wrong corner of the room, and I'd rather you went to him than waited for him to come to me. Go back into Ragefire Chasm, in the south-west corner of the city, past the Invoker's ritual hall to his walkway, and cut through his Searing Blade Fanatics to reach him.
org_sinister_edge.accept_text: Take your time and your healers. A cult is a body, and Bazzalan is the knife it holds in the dark.
org_sinister_edge.turn_in_text:
You did more than bring his throne to dust. The Searing Blade's hold on my city is broken, at least for now.

Wear this with pride. The Horde remembers who stands in the dark so that others can sleep.

org_whispers_cleft.description: The Cleft of Shadow has always belonged to the quiet kind of orc. That doesn't mean it belongs to whoever claims the quiet. A cult calling itself the Searing Blade has been using the Cleft's back tunnels to run its ritual stock down into the chasm, and I'm not pleased. A thief has a code, and the code doesn't include sacrifices. Go in through the gate in the Cleft and take them as they come, the Searing Blade Cultists first, then the Fanatics who guard them, and the Invokers who command them.
org_whispers_cleft.accept_text: They hide behind candlelight, and you can use that. Put the candles out and they'll lose you.
org_whispers_cleft.turn_in_text:
Their whispers have gone quiet, and I'll be back to my usual clientele by dusk.

Here's a small thank-you from a very small ghost.

org_who_holds_the_floor.description: My report on the southern border now has a second page, and it's worse than the first. There's country beyond the range after all, there are tauren living on top of it, and between the Horde and the salt flats a people holds the only ground that connects anything to anything. They're the Galak, centaur but not Kolkar, a different stock with different manners, and by every account better organised than anything we've fought on this continent. The Warchief doesn't need their history, he needs their name and their numbers. Go down onto that floor and count the Galak Outriders, and count their Windcatchers separately, because a people who post weather-watchers have a plan.
org_who_holds_the_floor.accept_text: Write the numbers down as you go. I'd rather have your tally than your memory.
org_who_holds_the_floor.turn_in_text:
They're drilled, then, and they keep a pace. They don't break and they don't chase.

I'll write that down, and I'll be unpopular for it. Everyone upstairs wants to hear about savages.
